newsitem.title: USA: USDA proposes raising pork import assessments.
newsitem.headline: USDA proposes raising pork import assessments.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department said Tuesday that it is proposing to increase assessments on imported pork and pork products by eight-hundredths of a cent per lb, or nineteen-hundredths of a cent per kg.

USDA said the proposed increase reflects the 25 percent hike in hog prices paid at major U.S. markets last year. The rate of assessment, which was raised to 0.45 from 0.35 of one percent of market price effective Sept 3, 1995, remains unchanged.
"This proposed change will bring importer assessments more in line with those being paid by domestic producers," USDA's Agricultural Marketing Service Administrator Lon Hatamiya said in a release.
The import assessments are set by formula each year, based on U.S. market prices for hogs. Assessments on domestic and imported pork are authorized by law.
The proposed changes will appear in the Feb 26 Federal Register. USDA said it will accept comments through March 28.
